main.title: Roblox
main.summary: Roblox is an online platform where users make games in Roblox Studio and play creations shared by others.

cards.text: Roblox is an online game platform and creation system developed by Roblox Corporation. David Baszucki and Erik Cassel began developing it in 2004 and opened it to the public in 2006. Users can make their own games and play those published by other creators. By February 2025, the company reported 85.3 million daily active users, reflecting how far the platform had grown from its small beginnings.

The platform hosts millions of user-created games, created using Luau, a modified dialect of the programming language Lua and the platform's game engine, Roblox Studio. While Roblox is free-to-play, it features in-game purchases done through its virtual currency known as Robux, and game developers on the platform are able to create items that cost Robux. The platform hosts a large virtual economy centered around those items and Robux. Using the platform's Developer Exchange program, creators are able to exchange their earned Robux for real-world currency. The platform has been used to host virtual concerts and events, as well as advergames.

While Roblox started off small—both in playerbase and as a company—it began to grow rapidly in the second half of the 2010s. This growth was further accelerated by the COVID-19 pandemic. By 2020, over 5,000 games on Roblox had been played over a million times, and over 20 had been played over one billion times. Although critic reviews for Roblox have been positive, it has faced criticism concerning child safety and its content moderation, due to material pornographic or politically extremist in nature. It has been criticized for its alleged exploitative practices toward children and microtransactions. The platform has been restricted or completely blocked in several countries, including China, Egypt, Turkey, and Iraq.

main.title: Test Drive Unlimited
main.summary: Test Drive Unlimited is a 2006 racing video game developed by Eden Games for Xbox 360 and Windows, with Atari Melbourne House developing the PlayStation 2 and PlayStation Portable versions, and published by Atari.

cards.heading: An open-road version of Oʻahu
cards.text: Atari published Test Drive Unlimited in 2006, with Eden Games developing the Xbox 360 and Windows editions and Atari Melbourne House handling PlayStation 2 and PSP. The game models the Hawaiian island of O?ahu as an open driving environment, with over 1,000 miles of roads and highways. Its licensed sports cars and motorcycles turn travel around the island into the basis of a new direction for the Test Drive series.

cards.heading: Sequels and a later reboot
cards.text: It was followed by a sequel, Test Drive Unlimited 2, in 2011. A third game and soft reboot, Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown, was released in 2024.

main.title: Company of Heroes
main.summary: Company of Heroes is a 2006 real-time strategy video game developed by Relic Entertainment and published by THQ for Windows and Mac OS X operating systems.

cards.heading: Relic brings strategy to the Normandy campaign
cards.text: Company of Heroes is Relic Entertainment's 2006 real-time strategy game, published by THQ. Its Second World War battles centre on capturing territory and using its resources to support troops and vehicles. It began the Company of Heroes series and was the first title to carry the Games for Windows label.

cards.heading: Capturing sectors to supply the army
cards.text: Company of Heroes is set during the Second World War and contains two playable factions. Players aim to capture strategic resource sectors located around the map, which they use to build base structures, produce new units, and defeat their enemies. In the single-player campaign the player commands two U.S. military units during the Battle of Normandy (Operation Overlord) and the liberation of France (Operation Cobra). Depending on the mission, the player controls either Able Company of the 29th Infantry Division's 116th Infantry, or Fox Company of the 101st Airborne Division's 506th PIR.

cards.heading: Awards, expansions and an online experiment
cards.text: Company of Heroes received widespread acclaim, winning multiple awards for the best strategy game of the year, and being considered one of the best video games ever made. Two expansions were released: Opposing Fronts in 2007 and Tales of Valor in 2009. A free-to-play massively multiplayer online version of the game, Company of Heroes Online, was briefly released as an open beta in South Korea in April 2010, before being cancelled in March 2011.

cards.heading: The game reaches tablets and Switch
cards.text: An iPad version, developed and published by Feral Interactive, was released in February 2020. A version for Android and iOS mobile devices was released in September 2020. A Nintendo Switch version was released on October 12, 2023.

cards.heading: Sequels and a film adaptation
cards.text: The success of the game led to a sequel, Company of Heroes 2, which was released in 2013. As of January 2013, the Company of Heroes series has sold more than 4 million copies. A film adaptation, also titled Company of Heroes, was released in 2013. The latest installment in the series, Company of Heroes 3, released in February 2023.

main.title: Ridge Racer 2
main.subtitle: A portable tour through Ridge history
main.summary: Namco Bandai released Ridge Racer 2 for PSP in Japan on 14 September 2006, under the name Ridge Racers 2. This is the handheld sequel, not the 1994 arcade game with the same Western title. Its 42 course layouts include forward and reverse directions, revisiting roads from earlier Ridge Racer games. Drifting does more than carry a car around a bend: it charges nitro, turning each corner into preparation for a later burst of speed. World Tours organises that familiar arcade pleasure into a succession of events, with new tours, cars and courses to unlock.

cards.heading: Drift, charge, release

cards.heading: More ways to chase the next corner
cards.text: Alongside World Tours and Time Attack, the sequel adds Arcade, Duel and Survival modes. Arcade uses checkpoint time limits, Duel pits two cars against one another, and Survival eliminates the last-place driver after each lap. Wireless Battle supports up to eight nearby PSPs. Its 42 racing pieces include twelve new recordings. The fifteen-track soundtrack album combines these additions with opening, menu and ending music; it later received an official digital release in 2024.

main.title: God Hand
main.summary: God Hand is a 2006 beat 'em up game developed by Clover Studio and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2.

cards.text: God Hand is a 2006 beat 'em up game developed by Clover Studio and published by Capcom for the PlayStation 2. It was released in Japan and North America in 2006, and in 2007 for PAL territories. It was re-released for the PlayStation 3 as a PS2 Classics downloadable game on the PlayStation Network on October 4, 2011. The game was directed by Shinji Mikami, who desired to create the game for hardcore gamers intermixed with a large amount of comic relief. It initially received a mixed response from critics and sold only modestly upon its release in Japan. It was Clover Studio's final video game. Retrospectively, the game has been received more positively and is considered a cult classic.

The game mixes western and Japanese-themed comedy, containing over-the-top characters and storyline events. The gameplay includes traditional elements of the beat 'em up genre with new features, these include being able to map and string together a large repertoire of fighting techniques to the gamepad's face buttons in order to create unique combo attacks. The plot follows a martial artist protecting his companion and wielding a legendary divine arm called the "God Hand", in order to save the world from demons.

main.title: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl
main.subtitle: Sinnoh opens the main series to the Nintendo DS
main.summary: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl take Game Freak's main series to Nintendo DS. Released in Japan on 28 September 2006, the paired games introduce Sinnoh and its new species. A trip to a lake with a childhood friend leads to an unexpected battle and a first partner, setting the player on a journey through Gyms and Team Galactic's activities.

cards.heading: A first partner beside the lake
cards.text: Pokémon Diamond and Pearl take Game Freak's main series to Nintendo DS. Released in Japan on 28 September 2006, the paired games introduce Sinnoh and its new species. A trip to a lake with a childhood friend leads to an unexpected battle and a first partner, setting the player on a journey through Gyms and Team Galactic's activities.

cards.heading: Routes through Sinnoh
cards.text: Sinnoh's routes lead between towns, lakes and the mountain at the region's centre. The rival repeatedly crosses the player's path, while Professor Rowan's research gives catching and studying Pokémon an ongoing purpose. Choosing a team means balancing creatures found along these routes with the opponents ahead. Team Galactic's interference brings another set of problems into the trip, connecting local encounters to the region's legendary Pokémon.

cards.heading: A second screen in the journey
cards.text: The DS separates the view of the adventure from information and commands on its lower screen. In battles, a touch selects actions while the upper display keeps the opponents visible. The Pokétch gathers tools such as a clock and party information into a device carried through the journey. These functions make the hardware part of the repeated rhythm of travel: checking, choosing and then returning attention to the route.

cards.heading: Partners across a network
cards.text: Wireless communication broadens how players can meet, exchange and battle. At release, Nintendo Wi-Fi Connection also made distant play possible, extending the social side of the paired games beyond people standing nearby. Version-specific encounters still give players a reason to compare their parties. The collection can hold the trace of another trainer's journey, bringing a creature from a different cartridge into battles and discoveries that continue on the player's own screen.

main.title: Project Sylpheed
main.subtitle: A rookie pilot inside a crowded space war
main.summary: Project Sylpheed is Game Arts and SETA's Xbox 360 space-combat game, first released in Japan on 28 September 2006. The player flies the Delta Saber through a campaign set during an interstellar civil war, confronting fighter formations and much larger capital ships. It revisits the name and spirit of Silpheed while allowing movement in any direction instead of following the earlier series' scrolling route. A mission can fill the surrounding space with targets, making the first task one of orientation: find the important threat and understand where the player's ship belongs within the battle.

cards.heading: Equip the fighter for the mission ahead
cards.text: Weapons and augmentations change how the Delta Saber handles a particular assignment. Some objectives ask for enemy targets to be destroyed; others require friendly ships to remain alive. Secondary goals add further conditions, such as completing a task quickly or avoiding damage. The player has to read the mission as more than a collection of hostile objects. Protecting something can require abandoning a tempting target elsewhere, while a carefully selected weapon can make the necessary intervention more effective. Preparation and awareness work together to keep a large encounter under control.

cards.heading: A cinematic successor with a different perspective
cards.text: Shinobu Gotou directed the sixteen-mission campaign, with animated scenes connecting the operations to its cast and political conflict. The score includes contributions from several Square Enix composers, among them Junya Nakano and Kumi Tanioka. Microsoft published the international editions in 2007. Critical responses varied between enthusiasm for its cinematic action and frustration with its complexity. The game offers a way to skip a mission after repeated failures, allowing the story to continue. Its distinctive ambition is to make a freely moving fighter feel like one small part of a much larger space battle.

main.title: Tenchu Z
main.subtitle: The ninja is someone the player creates
main.summary: Tenchu Z is K2's Xbox 360 stealth-action game, first released in Japan as Tenchu Senran on 5 October 2006. The player creates a new recruit of the Azuma Ninja Clan rather than selecting an established hero. Rikimaru gives assignments as Lord Gohda's domain approaches conflict with neighbouring Ogawara. Assassinations, rescues and the recovery of stolen objects provide different objectives within fifty missions. The created ninja develops through that work, connecting the series' quiet approaches and sudden attacks to a character whose appearance and abilities belong to the player's own campaign.

cards.heading: The ninja is someone the player creates
cards.text: Tenchu Z is K2's Xbox 360 stealth-action game, first released in Japan as Tenchu Senran on 5 October 2006. The player creates a new recruit of the Azuma Ninja Clan rather than selecting an established hero. Rikimaru gives assignments as Lord Gohda's domain approaches conflict with neighbouring Ogawara. Assassinations, rescues and the recovery of stolen objects provide different objectives within fifty missions. The created ninja develops through that work, connecting the series' quiet approaches and sudden attacks to a character whose appearance and abilities belong to the player's own campaign.

cards.heading: A successful mission improves the next infiltration
cards.text: Strength, agility and health can be adjusted, while gold earned through strong performances buys abilities, items and new visual options. Special attacks and editable combinations provide further ways to shape the character. Preparation therefore reaches beyond choosing the next destination. The player develops a ninja suited to a preferred approach, then has to make those choices work within the mission's objectives and patrols. The relationship between stealth and reward gives an efficient assignment continuing value, as the resources earned can improve the equipment and skills available when the next infiltration begins.

cards.heading: Stealth becomes a shared assignment
cards.text: Four-player cooperative play through Xbox Live allows several created ninjas to undertake missions together. That changes the familiar solitary infiltration into something whose approaches can be shared, with each participant bringing a developed character to the assignment. Kiyoji Tomita directed the game, published internationally by Microsoft in 2007. Returning figures such as Rikimaru maintain the link to earlier Tenchu adventures, while the custom protagonist and cooperative structure distinguish this entry. Tenchu Z's central shift is to make the role of ninja an identity built through repeated work rather than one inherited entirely from a predetermined hero.

main.title: The Legend of Spyro: A New Beginning
main.summary: A new origin story puts elemental attacks and close combat at the centre of Spyro's journey to the dragon guardians.

cards.heading: The game
cards.text: The Legend of Spyro: A New Beginning is Krome Studios' 2006 action adventure for PlayStation 2, Xbox and GameCube. It starts a new telling of Spyro's origins, following the young dragon from the swamp where he grew up towards the guardians threatened by Cynder. Combat and developing elemental powers give this journey its main structure.

cards.heading: Keep the enemy in reach
cards.text: A close encounter can move from a ground combo into an aerial attack. Knocking an enemy upwards opens a short opportunity to follow and continue the blows before it falls. Breath attacks can interrupt or damage opponents, while the enemies still standing make it dangerous to focus on only one target. The player alternates between those tools rather than treating every fight as the same charge. The result gives Spyro's small body a more physical role in the action.

cards.heading: Give a breath a different job
cards.text: Fire, electricity, ice and earth provide different attacks as the journey continues. Energy limits their use, and gems gained during the adventure replenish resources or help develop abilities. Choosing an upgrade gives a preferred attack more room in the next encounter. Fury adds a larger burst after its meter has been built, making timing important: spending it when surrounded can clear an opening, while saving it leaves the current fight to Spyro's regular moves and remaining breath energy.

cards.heading: Learn what the guardians can teach
cards.text: The dragon guardians connect these powers to the story. Reaching another elder brings instruction as well as another part of the struggle against Cynder, so the journey repeatedly moves from learning an ability to using it under pressure. Flying passages and large confrontations change the scale around those fights. Spyro's growing knowledge of his origins runs alongside the player's growing command of his attacks, with each new element providing another way to approach the next group of enemies.

main.title: Bully
main.summary: Bully (released in the PAL region as Canis Canem Edit; Latin for 'dog eat dog') is a 2006 action-adventure video game developed by Rockstar Vancouver and published by Rockstar Games.

cards.heading: Jimmy Hopkins arrives at Bullworth
cards.text: Bully (released in the PAL region as Canis Canem Edit; Latin for 'dog eat dog') is a 2006 action-adventure video game developed by Rockstar Vancouver and published by Rockstar Games. Set in the fictional New England town of Bullworth, the game follows juvenile delinquent student Jimmy Hopkins, who is involuntarily enrolled at Bullworth Academy, the town's prestigious boarding school. Over the course of a school year, Jimmy attempts to rise through the ranks of the school system to end bullying, while clashing with fellow students and authority figures.

cards.heading: Classes, cliques and two-player contests
cards.text: The game is played from a third-person perspective and its open world can be navigated on foot, skateboard, motor scooter, bicycle, or go-kart. Players control Jimmy as he attempts to become more popular among the school's various "cliques", in addition to attending classes and completing various side missions. The Scholarship Edition includes a two-player multiplayer mode that lets two players compete for the highest score in different classes.

cards.heading: From controversy to later editions
cards.text: Bully's expected violence and sexual content were initially controversial. The game was released on 17 October 2006 for the PlayStation 2 to positive reviews, with praise directed at its missions, narrative, characters, and soundtrack. It sold over 1.5 million copies and received multiple year-end accolades. A remastered version, subtitled Scholarship Edition, was developed by Mad Doc Software and released on 4 March 2008 for Xbox 360 and Wii, and on 21 October 2008 for Windows. Bully was re-released for the PlayStation 4, available via the PlayStation Network, on 22 March 2016. An updated version of the Scholarship Edition, titled Anniversary Edition, was developed by War Drum Studios and released for Android and iOS on 8 December 2016.
